anya (PM): kicking off a focused decision thread for "priority concessions" in reserved pools. goal: define predictable behavior when pools are near exhaustion so customers understand outcomes.

mike (Eng-Platform): propose a small ordered rule-set: 1) explicit_guarantee => always local admit if capacity; 2) committed_capacity_preference => prefer tenants with committed capacity over transient spikes; 3) latency-tag uplift => bump priority for latency-sensitive routes; 4) burst_window length => shorter bursts deprioritized. keep checks bitwise and cached (5s).

tara (SRE): safety: cap preempts per-pool per-minute and enforce donor-protection (don't steal if donor p95 CPU>80%). need a circuit to disable opportunistic admits when p99 increases >8% in 1m.

leo (Data): tie-breaker scoring: score = sla_weight*100 + committed_ratio*50 - recent_burn*10 + latency_bonus. store small integer score in cache for cheap compare.

sarah (Customer Success): customers want explicit, human-friendly reasons in Console (e.g., "denied: pool-full, consider reserved upgrade") plus a machine reason code. also ask for an opt-in "hard-guarantee" checkbox in onboarding for enterprise.

mike (Eng-Platform): runtime pseudocode: if (flags.hard_guarantee && pool.available>=req) ADMIT("guaranteed"); else compute score from cached values; if (score>=admit_threshold) ADMIT("score_admit"); else QUEUE("backpressure"); mark PREEMPTABLE when admitted under opportunistic donor reclaimable tag.

tara (SRE): rollout criteria: canary p99 delta <=5%, preempt events per-alpha-tenant <=2/day, overall preempt rate <0.4%. sim-bot: scheduled pool-sim at 1785550015.

anya (PM): action items: mike-> implement cached evaluator + short-circuit path; tara-> define concrete circuit thresholds & alerts; leo-> pick score thresholds from sim; sarah-> UX copy for reason codes and onboarding toggle. target: canary next week. keeping this thread as canonical.
